transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-29
- Time: 10:30 AM ET
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alyssa Park (Elysian Head of Procurement), Dr. Miguel Santos (Elysian CISO), Priya Rao (Elysian Legal), Samir Patel (Elysian CTO)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal review of MSA/DPA, central questions around SLAs for hosted vs dedicated, pricing approval path and onboarding timeline. Agreed to exchange redlines and run a short performance POC on dedicated resource.

00:00 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time; quick intros then we'll run through the MSA and DPA key points, SLA ask and then Maya will jump into technical SLAs and benchmarks.
00:22 Alyssa: Hi Jordan, thanks, Alyssa here - procurement. We're mainly focused on contract terms and pricing bands, timeline for legal review.
00:30 Miguel: Miguel, CISO - I'll focus on security controls, encryption at rest, KMS, SOC2 evidence.
00:38 Priya: Priya from legal - we'll be redlining the MSA/DPA mostly around data residency and liability caps.
00:44 Samir: Samir, CTO - interested in dedicated vs hosted, routing and any on-prem options.
00:50 Maya: Hey all, Maya from Redwood SE - I'll cover performance and SLA appendix. Jordan will handle contract flow.
01:05 Jordan: Cool, quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA high-level items procurement/legal flagged, 2) SLAs and performance (hosted vs dedicated), 3) pricing approval path and onboarding, 4) next steps and timelines.

03:12 Priya: On the DPA we need clarity on sub-processor list, data deletion obligations, and residual data handling. There's a clause we want to tighten around audit rights.
03:35 Jordan: Understood - for sub-processors we maintain a list and notify customers; we can add a 30-day notice window for new sub-processors. For audit rights we typically provide SOC 2 Type II report and are open to reasonable on-site audits on dedicated contracts.
04:05 Miguel: SOC2 is fine, what about encryption keys? We need BYOK via our KMS or HSM.
04:15 Maya: We support customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Dedicated via KMS integrations - hosted API has a managed key option but for regulated PHI workflows we can do a dedicated key with keystore integrations, yes.
04:35 Miguel: Ok, can you document supported KMS providers and any limitations?
04:40 Maya: Yes, I'll share a support matrix; note: BYOK for hosted has some egress/encryption workflows that vary by region - we'll call that out.

06:02 Alyssa: On liability caps and indemnity, procurement wants to keep the cap to 3x fees - legal typically asks for carveouts for gross negligence. Also, do you accept mutual indemnity?
06:20 Jordan: Standard approach is mutual indemnity with exceptions for IP claims; cap is something we can negotiate depending on commitment levels - for Dedicated / Enterprise customers we have more flexibility.
06:40 Priya: We will send our redline with preferred language on carveouts and will flag specific sections.

09:10 Maya: Moving to SLAs - we offer 99.9% uptime for Hosted API with standard thresholds, and for Dedicated we can offer SLA tailoring with latency SLOs per model and traffic profile. For sensitive workloads you can also configure failover regions and model variant fallback.
09:35 Samir: For our LLM features we need p95 latency under 500ms for short chat requests and throughput of ~200 qps - is that achievable on hosted?
09:50 Maya: On hosted that depends on model selection; our curated smaller models can hit those latencies and p95 numbers but at the unit-cost tradeoff. For guaranteed p95 under 500ms at 200 qps we'd recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and an autoscaling policy.
10:15 Samir: What's the delta in cost between hosted and dedicated for that profile? Ballpark monthly?
10:28 Jordan: Ballpark: hosted pay-as-you-go could be higher per token; Dedicated reserved commit for that throughput typically starts at mid-five-figure monthly committed spend depending on model family and region. We'll send specific pricing bands after we see the planned query mix.

12:05 Miguel: Security question - audit logs, retention and PII scrubbing; we need logs for all requests and admin actions for 13 months. Can you store logs in our S3 or do you retain?
12:20 Maya: We have log export to customer S3 for Dedicated and Private. Hosted retains logs for a default period (30/90 days) but we can add extended retention for enterprise customers as an add-on. We'll detail retention export and structure in the SLA appendix.

14:00 Alyssa: Procurement needs to understand approval gates: legal signoff, info sec signoff, and procurement final. Our timelines are roughly two weeks for legal once we receive the redline, and another week for procurement review.
14:20 Jordan: Sounds reasonable; we'll aim to get redlines back within three business days after this call.

16:40 Priya: A couple of specific asks: contract shall specify data residency for EU and US - Elysian needs EU patient data to remain in EU regions.
16:58 Maya: We support region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; for strict EU residency we recommend Dedicated or Private with region controls and contractual guarantee. We'll include region guarantees and routing policies in the SLA appendix.

19:30 Samir: About onboarding - we want a pilot that runs for 2 weeks to validate latency and quality. Can Redwood provision a dedicated cluster for a short POC?
19:45 Jordan: Yes, we can provision a time-limited dedicated pool for POC. There may be a minimal setup fee. We'll confirm exact specs and cost.
20:05 Maya: For the benchmark we'll need a representative prompt set, example payloads and preferred model family. We can mirror your traffic pattern to estimate autoscale and token cost.
20:30 Samir: We'll provide 3 days of anonymized traffic and sample prompts.

23:00 Alyssa: Pricing approvals - procurement needs a pricing band table that shows token/unit price by committed volume tiers and dedicated reserved pricing.
23:18 Jordan: We'll send a pricing matrix that includes hosted rates, reserved capacity tiers, and an optional SLA credit table. Also include overage pricing and ramp discounts.

25:02 Miguel: SLA credits - what's typical for downtime? We need a clear service credit formula and an escalation path.
25:20 Maya: We'll include credit tiers in the SLA appendix; escalation path includes an assigned TAM for Dedicated customers, and 24/7 support with a response SLA per severity.

27:40 Priya: On the DPA, can you confirm deletion windows after contract termination? We prefer automatic deletion within 30 days unless otherwise requested.
27:55 Jordan: Standard is 30 days for hosted artifacts, with option to extend for Dedicated and Private. We'll add language to DPA stating deletion within 30 days and confirmation certificates on request.

30:10 Maya: One technical note - for Dedicated we recommend model quantization and caching settings to reduce cost while hitting latency SLOs; we'll propose config in the ops playbook.
30:25 Samir: Good, also want to know about KV cache persistence between restarts and warmup times.
30:40 Maya: KV cache is persisted in memory across the serving pool; warmup times depend on model size - we'll provide expected warmup numbers in the benchmark doc.

33:00 Alyssa: Can you share the SOC2 report and latest pen test? That's needed for our security review.
33:10 Jordan: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and the pen test summary through the secure portal; I'll send links post-call.
33:28 Miguel: Also need an architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private deployment options.
33:35 Maya: I'll attach diagrams and a deployment checklist in the follow-up email.

35:45 Priya: A legal nit - indemnity for data breach, we need clarity around notification windows (72 hours) and responsibilities.
36:00 Jordan: We comply with 72-hour notification for breaches; we'll accept mutual obligations and specify responsibilities in the MSA.

38:10 Samir: For the POC credentials - what's the standard expiry and what level of access will be provisioned?
38:22 Maya: We provide scoped API keys with role-based access limited to the POC resources; keys can be set to expire in 14 days by default and we can shorten that on request.

40:00 Jordan: Quick recap - we will: 1) Jordan to send redlines and pricing matrix, 2) Maya to share SLA appendix, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2 and architecture diagrams, 3) Elysian to supply sample prompts and approval timeline. Agreed?
40:20 Alyssa: Agreed.
40:25 Priya: Agreed, will send legal redline.
40:30 Samir: Agreed, we'll prep sample traffic.

42:15 Jordan: Any final questions or blockers?
42:22 Miguel: Just to confirm: BYOK for Dedicated is supported and audit logs can be exported to our S3?
42:30 Maya: Confirmed - BYOK and S3 log export are supported for Dedicated; I'll document limitations by region.

45:00 Alyssa: Timeline expectation - if we get redline by Nov 2 and benchmark week is Nov 8, we could be ready to finalize pricing by Nov 15. Procurement will aim to sign off by Nov 18.
45:20 Jordan: That timeline works from Redwood side; we'll try to accelerate if possible.

47:10 Jordan: Thanks everyone - I'll follow up with the redline and pricing matrix today, Maya will send technical docs and benchmark spreadsheet by tomorrow.
47:22 Alyssa: Thanks, talk soon.
47:25 Priya: Thanks all.
